titulo: Move the problem out of your ears
subtitulo: Repeat, slow down, write it and show it on the map — the repair ladder for a noisy counter
cena: The departure time just went past you for the second time, said fast and confident, and the queue behind you is not getting any shorter.

steps.pt: The false smile-and-nod inherits the wrong problem. The ladder: say the break, ask slower, get it written, use the map.
I didn't understand.

steps.promptPt: At a noisy counter, the attendant gives you a long answer and you lose it. Stop the false smile and say you didn't understand. Speak now.
steps.pt: I didn't understand.
Sorry? What was that?
Here's the frame: ¿me puede, then the thing you need done. Recognise mande too — no need to copy it.

steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-deh reh-peh-TEER mahs dehs-PAH-syoh
steps.pt: Can you repeat that more slowly?

steps.promptPt: The bus attendant repeats at the same speed. Ask for the whole thing again, more slowly. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-deh reh-peh-TEER mahs dehs-PAH-syoh
steps.pt: Can you repeat that more slowly?

steps.es: Claro. Sale a las quince cincuenta.
steps.pt: Of course. It leaves at 15:50.
steps.tts: Claro. Sale a las quince cincuenta.

steps.pt: Slower can still fail on numbers, names, addresses. Stop spending listening attempts — put it somewhere your eyes can hold.

steps.promptPt: You still cannot separate quince from cincuenta. Ask the attendant to write the departure time. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-deh ehs-kree-BEER, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Can you write it down for me, please?
Yes, of course. 15:50.
Last channel: the map. A written street name can still leave three branches unclear — open the map and ask for the point.

steps.promptPt: A local writes the street name, but you still do not know which branch it is. Open the map and ask them to show you. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh MWEHS-trah en el MAH-pah
steps.pt: Can you show me on the map?

steps.es: Sí. Es aquí, después de la esquina.
steps.pt: Yes. It's here, after the corner.
steps.tts: Sí. Es aquí, después de la esquina.

steps.promptPt: Same frame, new action: ask them to slow the whole conversation down. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you speak more slowly?

steps.promptPt: It is a name and you need the letters. Keep the frame, change the action. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you spell it for me?

steps.promptPt: A phone number just went past you. Ask for it in writing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you write the number down?

steps.promptPt: Only the address was lost, not the whole answer. Ask for just that. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you repeat the address?

steps.es: No entendí. ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio? ¿Me lo puede escribir?
steps.pinyin: noh en-ten-DEE. meh loh PWEH-deh reh-peh-TEER mahs dehs-PAH-syoh. meh loh PWEH-deh ehs-kree-BEER
steps.pt: Shadow the first three rungs without adding an apology.
steps.tts: No entendí. ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio? ¿Me lo puede escribir?

steps.pt: B03 complete. Say the break, slow the repeat, write it, point to the map — the ladder stays in Spanish the whole time.

aprofundar.titulo: Repair is a change of channel

secoes.corpo: Start with the smallest repair that can work. If slower repetition succeeds, stop. Move to writing only for payloads that remain fragile: numbers, names, addresses, medicine and times.
In Mexico, ¿mande? can be a courteous response when somebody calls or was not heard. Treat it as 'sorry?' in this lesson. Recognition is useful; imitation is optional.
A third identical listening attempt rarely changes the result. Writing externalises the detail and gives both people the same object to verify.

exemplos.pt: Can you write it down for me?
Can you show me on the map?

permissao: You are allowed to say 'no entendí' and mean it plainly, with no apology attached. Losing the thread in a noisy counter is not a failure of your Spanish — it is a normal part of a real conversation, and the ladder exists precisely so you never have to fake understanding to keep things moving.
espelho: A tourist speaking English abroad does the same false-smile nod when they lose the thread of a fast reply, and it produces exactly the same downstream mess — the wrong platform, the wrong price, the wrong turn. The habit is not a Spanish-specific weakness; it is what anyone does under the small social pressure of not wanting to seem slow, in any language.
frasePiso: When listening fails, change the channel before you change the language.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You nod and say gracias to an answer you did not actually catch, and ten minutes later you are on the wrong platform or paying the wrong amount.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I didn't want to hold up the line, or I didn't want to look like my Spanish wasn't good enough to follow a simple answer.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The nod protects the conversation for exactly one more second and then hands you a real problem later, at a moment when the original speaker is gone and cannot help you fix it.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say no entendí immediately, in the same breath as the nod you were about to give, before you walk away with a guess.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The correction happens while the person who has the answer is still standing in front of you, which is the only moment it is free.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not as a substitute for trying at all — saying no entendí to every sentence without ever attempting the exchange reads as giving up, not as repair.

clique.desconto: Nobody gave you three different sentences for three different breakdowns. You kept one opening — ¿me puede — and changed only the thing you needed done.
clique.piso: Next time an answer goes past you, you won't nod and hope. You'll pick the repair you need and ask for that one.
